firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Sharing a small resource that may help teams tune their agents' first few tool calls. For each of the 129 public tasks I mapped the reference patch onto the call-graph node(s) it changes (a "gold edit site"), then measured how well three model-free signals rank that node: TF-IDF keywords from the report, the provided embeddings (queried via symbols named in the report, as search_similar_code does offline), and hop distance in the provided call graph.

Headline numbers on the 117 tasks with a gold node in the graph: keyword Hit@5 14.5%, embeddings 25.6%, reciprocal-rank fusion 30.8% (random would be 5.9%). The edit site is within 2 hops of a symbol mentioned in the report in 47.9% of tasks, and the 2-hop neighbourhood shrinks the search from ~3,200 functions to a median of 80. Only 28% of reports name the exact function, but 73% name some symbol in the graph, which is why the graph helps. fastapi is much harder than rich or requests on every signal. Bootstrap CIs and a pairwise ablation are in the notebook.

Per-task CSV (gold-site counts, Hit@k per signal, hop distance, difficulty label) and all code, CPU-only, about eight minutes: https://www.kaggle.com/code/alikalwar/code-graph-bug-localization-benchmark-gemma-4-pap

Happy to hear what localization signals others have found useful, and whether the hard split lines up with your agents' failures.
